task: Task 6 — batched-path cost / latency / scale on multi-batch documents

\u26a0\ufe0f_CORPUS_TIER.tier: _trimmed — NOT the full published PDF, but 100% of the standards
\u26a0\ufe0f_CORPUS_TIER.detail: The run_id is `full08292026` and that name is WRONG: neither execution processed the full published PDF. Verified two independent ways (Step Functions execution input names the file; PyMuPDF gives the page count): KY ran kentucky_all_standards_2021_trimmed.pdf (52pp) rather than kentucky_all_standards_2021.pdf (120pp), and CO ran colorado_3_5_trimmed_2020.pdf (41pp) rather than colorado_birth_to_8_2020.pdf (187pp).
\u26a0\ufe0f_CORPUS_TIER.\u26a0\ufe0f_page_ratio_is_not_a_coverag: CORRECTED 2026-08-31 by Emily, who performed the trimming: the _trimmed tier retains 100% OF THE STANDARDS. What was removed is non-standards matter — preamble, introductions, guiding-principles essays, appendices, acknowledgements. The first version of this manifest read 52/120 and 41/187 as coverage fractions (43% / 22%) and framed full-document scale as a stated coverage limitation. Both readings are WITHDRAWN. Corroborated by this recording's own integrity checks: 50 of KY's 52 pages and 37 of CO's 41 carry detected elements, and every gap was read and confirmed content-free.
\u26a0\ufe0f_CORPUS_TIER.\u26a0\ufe0f_colorado_qualification: CO's 41pp is not a trim at all: corpus_tiers.json records the full Ages 3-5 document as 41pp, the same number. The 187pp birth-to-8 file is the WIDER PUBLICATION the Ages 3-5 band is drawn from (its TOC puts 'Ages 3-5' at p77; the 3-5 file's p3 is that document's p113 verbatim). Every CO golden and every CO number in the paper is the Ages 3-5 band, so coverage is complete within the scope the paper measures; the birth-to-3 and 5-8 bands are out of scope, not trimmed away.
\u26a0\ufe0f_CORPUS_TIER.guardrail_1: EVERY table built from this recording must be labelled _trimmed tier — it is neither _only_subset nor the full published PDF — AND must say what that tier means (complete standards content, non-standards matter removed). A bare '_trimmed' label reads as 'excerpt' and puts a false coverage claim in the paper.
\u26a0\ufe0f_CORPUS_TIER.what_remains_a_limitation: Page-count scale, which is a cost/batching question rather than a coverage one. These runs exercise 18 and 17 detection chunks over 4 Map iterations. A document with its non-standards matter left in, or a larger standards corpus such as AZ (217pp published), would chunk further and cost proportionally more, so the per-document token/latency figures here must not be extrapolated to untrimmed page counts.
\u26a0\ufe0f_CORPUS_TIER.still_valid: Task 6 step 2 asks for 'at least one full OR _trimmed document through the batched production path', so this satisfies the task as written — and, given complete standards coverage, more strongly than first recorded.

integrity_checks._why: A green Step Functions status proves nothing here — CLAUDE.md documents a run that reported SUCCEEDED while 31 of 52 pages had zero surviving coverage. All three documented silent-failure signatures were checked explicitly.

page_coverage.KY: 50 of 52 pages carry detected elements. Missing p1 (title page) and p14 (anecdote only) — both read and confirmed content-free.
page_coverage.CO: 37 of 41. Missing p1 (cover), p2 (section divider), p40 ('intentionally left blank'), p41 (acknowledgments) — all read and confirmed content-free.

pass1_depth_map.KY: 4 levels (domain > strand > sub_strand > indicator) — matches golden

batching_evidence._why_this_is_the_point: At the _only_subset tier every state produces <=5 chunks against MAX_CHUNKS_PER_BATCH=5 and <=3 domains against MAX_DOMAINS_PER_BATCH=3, so both batching layers collapse to a single batch, the Map has one iteration and the merge is a no-op. That is why the batching claim could not be supported by the subset-tier tables. These runs break that, which is what Task 6 existed to establish.

per_stage_metrics._units: Tokens are the primary hard number. USD is derived from BEDROCK_PRICING, every entry of which was confirmed against the AWS Bedrock pricing page (Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on 2026-08-31, Haiku 4.5 on 2026-09-04).

models_verified_at_runtime._note: All three have BEDROCK_PRICING entries, so the feared silent-$0 stage did NOT occur. Independently corroborated by CloudWatch list-metrics, which knows exactly these three model ids in this account over the trailing ~14 days.

\u26a0\ufe0f_how_these_numbers_were_OBTA.problem: Task 6 step 3 says to pull per-stage metrics from PipelineRunMetrics.summary(). That method NEVER RUNS: PipelineRunMetrics and log_pipeline_run_summary are defined in src/els_pipeline/metrics.py and referenced nowhere else in src/ (verified by grep, 2026-08-30). They are dead code. The Key Background section of tasking/arxiv_paper.md asserted 'cost data already exists' on this basis and has been corrected.
\u26a0\ufe0f_how_these_numbers_were_OBTA.method_actually_used: Per-call `LLM_METRICS:` log lines emitted by call_bedrock_llm, read from the stage Lambdas' CloudWatch log groups, cross-referenced against CloudTrail InvokeModel events for per-run attribution, and separated into stages BY model_id.
\u26a0\ufe0f_how_these_numbers_were_OBTA.why_by_model_id: `stage` is hardcoded to "detection" in detector.py:1235, so the Haiku depth-map call is logged as a detection call; and metrics_context is never passed at the real per-chunk detection call site (detection_batching.py:243) or per-domain parse call site (parse_batching.py:232), so run_id/state/batch_index are blank on every production line. Separating by model_id works only because the three stages happen to use three different models — it would break if two stages shared one.
\u26a0\ufe0f_how_these_numbers_were_OBTA.guardrail_6: This reconstruction method IS the regeneration procedure. Anyone reproducing these numbers must follow it, not step 3 as written.

cost_caveat.status: RESOLVED — all five BEDROCK_PRICING entries confirmed.
cost_caveat.detail: BEDROCK_PRICING is hardcoded as of April 2026 and none of its five entries could be confirmed on 2026-08-30. The AWS Price List API's AmazonBedrock service code catalogs only legacy Claude 2.x/3.x (confirmed against the full 1032-product bulk offer file); a second service code carries partial current-gen pricing but has no entry for Opus 4.6 or Sonnet 4.6, and its only Haiku 4.5 entry is a `mantle`-endpoint rate ~10% above the hardcoded one and for a different endpoint than the pipeline calls.
cost_caveat.action: Dollar figures are publishable with source and date cited. Tokens remain the primary hard number (Task 6 step 4).
cost_caveat.confirmed_by: Emily Cheyne against https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/: Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on 2026-08-31, Haiku 4.5 on 2026-09-04.

token_reconciliation.question: The day's account-wide Opus spend was 727,798 in / 198,073 out, while these two runs account for only 424,850 / 111,655. The gap prompted a suspicion of missing coverage.
token_reconciliation.answer: Closed with no residual. The remainder — 302,948 in / 86,418 out across 27 direct Opus calls — was made under the kinder-ready-dev-cli IAM user from a local machine between 10:15 and 10:59 -07:00, entirely BEFORE either execution started. Confirmed via CloudTrail InvokeModel events; the two pieces sum to the CloudWatch total exactly.
token_reconciliation.so_the_forecast_gap_was: not missing coverage, but a forecast scaled from PUBLISHED page counts (120pp and 187pp) rather than standards-content page counts (52pp and 41pp), plus an unrelated local Opus block earlier that morning.
